hook_text: Change one tiny number and water becomes PEROXIDE. Here's the illegal move.
clip_script: Learn the commandment that governs the whole craft: you may change only the coefficients — the big numbers written in front of formulas. You may never touch the subscripts inside a formula. A subscript defines a substance's identity: H2O — two hydrogens, one oxygen — is water. Change the subscript to H2O2 and you have not adjusted a count; you have manufactured a different substance — hydrogen peroxide, the antiseptic, not the drink. A coefficient, by contrast, is a multiplier of the whole formula. Coefficients change amounts without touching identities.
visual_style: A water molecule morphing horrifyingly into peroxide as a subscript edits, then snapping back as bold coefficients stamp down in front of formulas instead.
mood: Cautionary lab-drama with a confident fix.
pacing: Shock opening, firm commandment, brisk C-H-O worked balance to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and balance the propane equation in ninety seconds.
